newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble edges down in quiet Monday trade.
newsitem.headline: Rouble edges down in quiet Monday trade.

text.p: The rouble edged down in calm trade on Monday, and dealers said banks were investing cheap roubles in dollars.
"Roubles are cheap and banks prefer to buy dollars, but (Wednesday's) auctions could counterbalance the (dollar's) slow upward trend," United Investment Bank chief dealer Alexander Suchkov said.
On Wednesday, the central bank will auction eight trillion roubles of new six-month paper and an additional tranche of three trillion roubles of six-month bills.
Another dealer said the auctions were unlikely to soak up many roubles, and the dollar could edge up further over the next two days.

Roubles for today settlement were quoted at 5,489-91 per dollar compared with an early 5,488-91 and 5,487-90 late on Friday. Tomorrow roubles edged down to 5,489-92 per dollar from yesterday's late 5,488-90.
The central bank said it had set 5,481/5,491 as its bid and offer rates against the dollar on Monday.
Overnight rouble credits yielded 5-10 percent compared with an early 15-25 percent and Friday's late one to five percent.
